title: How Does Chunking Affect Retrieval-Augmented Code Completion? A Controlled Empirical Study

selection.evidence: NOTES: 'Chosen because the RAG area file flagged its Cliff's delta of exactly -1.0 as complete separation, worth chasing.'

cost.compute_notes: arXiv PDF (10 pp) read. Zenodo replication package chunk.zip 2,180,133 B (md5 85caa874d297e5a395d63f0059f5b999) from version record 19228778; the paper cites the CONCEPT DOI 19228777, which today resolves to the same single version. Statistics recomputed from the shipped result CSVs in seconds; the inference pipeline (vLLM, 5 generators) not re-run.

triggers: does chunking strategy matter for RAG code completion

claims.statement: Function-level chunking underperforms all other strategies by 3.57-5.64 pp EM on RepoEval (Cliff's delta = -1.0, large effect); pairwise Wilcoxon tests with Bonferroni correction are significant.
claims.scope: RepoEval API and line splits; 144 matched configurations per strategy (4 retrievers x 4 generators x 9 chunk-size/context settings); StarCoder2 excluded from RepoEval because its technical report has no RAG results there.

quantities.name: cliffs_delta_function_vs_others_true_unpaired
quantities.unit: Cliff's delta, P(x>y) - P(x<y) over 144 x 144 configuration pairs (API; -0.823/-0.847/-0.820 vs Declaration/Sliding/cAST)
quantities.baseline: line split: -0.766/-0.943/-0.937. The paper's -1.0 reproduces exactly as the PAIRED SIGN statistic (#x>y - #x<y)/n computed by the notebook's cliffs_delta()

quantities.name: paired_em_difference_function_minus_sliding_api
quantities.unit: EM percentage points, mean over 144 matched configurations

quantities.name: function_minus_sliding_em_cost_adjusted
quantities.unit: EM pp, OLS with generator x retriever FE and log2 token cost, cluster SE 0.17

quantities.name: paired_sign_function_vs_others_with_starcoder2
quantities.unit: paired sign statistic (API, vs Declaration), 180 configurations
quantities.baseline: -0.917 vs Sliding, -0.961 vs cAST: 'worse in every configuration' holds only with StarCoder2 excluded

our_assessment.why: The ranking is real and large: the true Cliff's delta is -0.82 to -0.94, 'large' by the usual thresholds, and Function is lower in all 144 matched configurations. But the -1.0 the abstract headlines is not Cliff's delta. The notebook function named cliffs_delta, commented 'for paired samples', computes the paired sign statistic; it then reads it against Cliff's delta thresholds. The notebook applies Holm correction where the text says Bonferroni. The Wilcoxon p-values (~1e-25) treat 144 configurations as independent units, although every configuration is scored on the same benchmark items. Configuration-level p-values say nothing about generalisation to new tasks, and no per-item outputs are shipped to compute item-level uncertainty. 'Worse in every configuration' also depends on excluding StarCoder2, which was excluded for a stated reason; with it included the sign statistic is -0.77 to -0.96. The authors' own explanation (function chunks are shorter than the smallest chunk size, so the token budget goes unused) predicts this ordering; their Pareto analysis, in which Function is never optimal even at its lower token cost, partly answers the budget confound.

claims.statement: (zoo reanalysis, not the authors' claim) The saturation size n* cannot be computed from Wu et al.'s tables with the independent-arms formula: across the 144-192 generator x retriever configurations the effects of chunking strategy and context length vary LESS than the independent-arms standard error of one configuration (observed SD 0.76-1.52 pp vs 1.75 pp), so tau^2 <= 0 and n* = infinity. Because the arms are paired (same 1,600 tasks), the true SE is smaller and only lower bounds follow: n* >= 2,143-8,606 tasks, all above the N = 1,600 evaluated.
claims.scope: RepoEval API and line splits, Exact Match; N = 1,600 tasks per split recovered from printed EM decimals (88% exactly k/1600 rounded half-up, the rest +0.0001). Lower bound uses observed SD as an upper bound on tau.

our_assessment.why: Contrast with the NQ-open Power-of-Noise multiverse, where specification dispersion dominates by 23-45x: here the chunking effect is STABLE across generators and retrievers, so the evaluation is below saturation and more tasks would still help. Two lessons. (1) n* is a property of a task x contrast, not of 'RAG'. (2) The formula as I wrote it in 2026-08 silently assumes independent arms; on a paired design with small tau it returns 0 dispersion (known-answer simulation in mazuryk2026-powerless-noise/reanalysis/07: true tau 0.005 -> independent estimate 0 in 48% of replicates). Without per-task outputs the bounds are all that is identifiable.

checked.how: curl api/records/19228777 -> 302 to 19228778; conceptrecid 19228777; one version; curl .../files/chunk.zip/content; md5sum; python reanalysis/w1_cliff.py
checked.result: md5 matches the record; configuration-level result CSVs (api/line_all_results.csv, 725 rows each) reproduce every value in eval/figure/output/repoeval_rq1_statistical_tests.csv once StarCoder2 is dropped as in the notebook. No per-item predictions shipped (examples/outputs holds 3 sample files).

relations.why: Both report effects over a grid of model/retriever/parameter configurations scored on one benchmark, and both treat configurations as the units of inference; the uncertainty that matters for a practitioner (over tasks) is not what the tests measure.

open_questions: Item-level reanalysis: needs per-task predictions (not shipped). Ask whether they exist.

ANSWERED 2026-10-16 (reanalysis/w2_budget.py): with generator x retriever fixed effects and log2(token cost), Function - Sliding goes from -3.96 to -3.50 pp (API) and -5.64 to -5.15 pp (line); a doubling of tokens is worth +2.4/+2.1 pp and Function uses ~15% fewer. The token budget explains ~10% of the deficit; the rest fits the authors' second explanation (function chunks drop module-level code), not their first.
